//: Until this file existed, every token rule docs/design-system/ states was unenforceable prose:
`npm run lint` is eslint over .js/.ts only, and `npm run format` never runs in CI.
'No hardcoded values' and 'border-radius: 0 always' have been in CLAUDE.md for the
life of the project with nothing checking either.
The cards are in scope too, via postcss-html. Without that the design system would
be the only CSS in the repo exempt from the design system's own rules.

color-no-hex.message: Use a token from design-tokens.css, not a raw hex value.

overrides.//: The token file IS where literal colours are defined. Exempting it is the point of having it.

//: docs/design-system/ cards are HTML with inline <style>. Their documentation chrome (.stage,
.list-frame, .readout) is not shipped UI, so it is not held to the erf- naming
rule below — but it IS held to the token rules, because a card that hardcodes a
colour to make a point is exactly how the wrong colour gets copied out of it.
Component CSS under docs/design-system/ is destined for src/. Every class is prefixed erf-.
Not cosmetic: Mermaid emits class="row" on gitGraph commit labels and on its
generic label path, and the app injects that SVG with innerHTML — so a bare
global .row would reach into diagram labels in the preview and in exported
images. That collision was found by luck, not by review.
Adopted files keep the rule when they move to src/. Scoping this to docs/design-system/ only would silently switch the guard off at the exact moment the CSS became shipping code.

selector-class-pattern.message: Design-system component classes must be namespaced erf- (see the Mermaid .row collision).

//: ScreenshotOverlay documents its token bypass deliberately (issue #164 / F[36]):
the overlay paints over arbitrary desktop content, so it needs fixed colours that
do not follow the app theme. A file-level exemption states that once, instead of
six line-level disables that each look like an oversight. Each site also carries a
`deviates:` marker and a row in the Colours card's Exceptions section.
Only colours are exempt: its corners are 0 like everywhere else, so the
border-radius rule applies to it.
--shadow-focus has no remaining use in src/ (#230), so its ban follows the
migration out of docs/design-system/. The four retired colours are still referenced in src/
and stay banned in docs/design-system/ only until their own migration lands.
The documentation trees are held to the token rules by MECHANISM, not by review: spacing, type and motion
values come from tokens, and no colour function appears at all. Scoped to docs/ only - the app's own CSS still
carries literals the design system has not decided yet, and switching these on repo-wide would be a red CI,
not a decision. A value a card is DECIDING may still be literal behind a stylelint-disable with a description.
Exempt from the docs-only rules above: the token copy (it IS where literals live), the @font-face file
(a descriptor names the face, not a token), and the adopted component CSS copied from src/ (it follows the src rules,
and an edit here would be overwritten by the next `npm run design`).
Retired tokens. Each is still referenced in src/, so a repo-wide ban would be a
red CI rather than a decision - it is enforced where the decision lives, and
follows into src/ with the migration. --shadow-focus is the sharpest case: over
--color-bg-primary it composites to 1.63:1, and a focus indicator needs 3:1, so
it cannot be one of the three competing focus-ring definitions at all.
docs/designs/ is held to the same ban: a feature screen copies from the cards, so a
retired token drawn there would be copied straight back into src/.
